outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Overview of Byte‑Level Language Modeling
outline.description: Introduces the fundamental challenges of tokenization, explains why byte‑level models are attractive, and presents the high‑level goals of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT).
subtopics: Limitations of conventional sub‑word tokenizers (domain bias, noise sensitivity, multilingual inequity)
Historical attempts at character/byte models and their scalability issues
Key idea of dynamic compute allocation via patches
Summary of BLT contributions

outline.chapter_title: From Bytes to Patches: Dynamic Segmentation Strategies
outline.description: Explains how raw byte streams are grouped into variable‑size patches, the mathematical formulation of patching functions, and compares different patching schemes.
subtopics: Formal definition of a patching function and its impact on FLOPs
Static (strided) patching and its drawbacks
Space‑based patching and linguistic intuition
Entropy‑based patching using a small byte‑level LM
Global vs. relative entropy thresholds, monotonic constraint
Incremental patching property and why BPE fails it
Comparison of BPE tokenization and patching

outline.chapter_title: BLT Architecture: Global Latent Transformer plus Local Encoders/Decoders
outline.description: Describes each component of the BLT model, how they interact, and why the three‑block design yields compute efficiency.
subtopics: Overall block diagram and data flow
Latent Global Transformer: architecture, block‑causal mask, role in compute budget
Local Encoder: lightweight transformer, cross‑attention pooling, hash‑n‑gram embeddings
Encoder hash‑n‑gram embedding details (hash function, n‑gram sizes, normalization)
Cross‑attention mechanism in the encoder (Perceiver‑style, patch‑specific masks)
Local Decoder: architecture, cross‑attention direction swap, byte generation
Decoder cross‑attention specifics
Why only the Global Transformer dominates FLOPs

outline.chapter_title: Training and Inference Efficiency: FLOP Accounting and Patch Size Trade‑offs
outline.description: Shows how to compute FLOPs for each component, how patch size controls cost, and how BLT achieves inference efficiency.
subtopics: Transformer FLOP formulas (feed‑forward, QKV, attention) and modifications for BLT
Cross‑attention FLOP cost derivation
Per‑byte FLOP computation and the role of average patch size
Entropy model training and lookup‑table optimization
Batch packing strategy for patches
Context‑length equalization across different patch sizes
Inference‑flop‑controlled scaling: fixing FLOP budget and varying model/patch size

outline.description: Presents the controlled scaling experiments, compares BLT with token‑based baselines, and interprets the results.
subtopics: Compute‑optimal scaling (parameter‑matched) methodology
Dataset mixes (Llama‑2 vs BLT‑1T) and training regimes
Training FLOPs vs Bits‑Per‑Byte curves for 1B–8B models
Impact of patch size (4.5 B, 6 B, 8 B) on scaling trends
Fixed‑inference‑budget experiments and crossover points
Analysis of why larger patches improve scaling (reduced Global steps)
Limitations of current scaling law extrapolation for BLT

outline.description: Covers the benchmark suite used to assess BLT, highlighting gains on reasoning, code generation, and robustness to noise.
subtopics: Evaluation tasks: classification (ARC, HellaSwag, PIQA, MMLU), code (MBPP, HumanEval)
Metrics: Accuracy, Pass@1, Bits‑Per‑Byte, BLEU for translation
Results: BLT‑Entropy vs Llama 3 on standard benchmarks
Robustness experiments: character‑level noise (AntSpeak, Drop, RandomCase, Repeat, UpperCase)
Character‑level tasks: G2P, CUTE benchmark, orthographic manipulation
Low‑resource machine translation results across 21 languages
Interpretation of why byte‑level modeling aids robustness and long‑tail generalization

outline.chapter_title: From Token Models to Byte‑Level: Distillation and Byte‑ifying
outline.description: Explains how pretrained token‑based LLMs can be leveraged to bootstrap BLT training, reducing compute requirements.
subtopics: Weight‑transfer of the Global Transformer from a pretrained Llama 3 model
Training schedule: frozen vs. fine‑tuned global weights, learning‑rate scaling for local modules
Empirical results: performance vs FLOPs compared to scratch‑trained BLT and token models
Discussion of converting a tokenizer‑based model into a tokenizer‑free one
Future directions for end‑to‑end learned patching

outline.description: Systematically evaluates the impact of each architectural and training decision on model quality.
subtopics: Entropy model size and context window impact on scaling
Comparison of all patching schemes (static, space, BPE‑derived, entropy)
Effect of cross‑attention placement and query initialization (learned, hash, pooled)
n‑gram hash embedding size vs. performance across domains
Local encoder/decoder layer depth trade‑offs
Interaction between patch size and cross‑attention benefits

outline.description: Places BLT within the broader literature on character‑level models, transformer‑based byte models, and patching methods.
subtopics: Early character‑level RNNs and CNNs
CharFormer, CANINE, ByT5, MambaByte – strengths and limitations
Patch‑based approaches: MegaByte, SpaceByte, hierarchical hourglass transformer
Comparison of BLT’s dynamic entropy patching to learned boundary predictors
How BLT advances the state of the art

outline.chapter_title: Practical Considerations, Limitations, and Future Work
outline.description: Discusses implementation challenges, current limitations of BLT, and promising research directions.
subtopics: Potential mismatch between Llama‑3 scaling laws and optimal BLT ratios
Library support: FlexAttention, FlashAttention, and wall‑clock efficiency
Scalability beyond 8B parameters and larger patch sizes
End‑to‑end learnable patching and joint entropy‑model training
Further robustness studies (adversarial noise, cross‑modal data)
Open‑source code and reproducibility notes

outline.description: Summarizes key takeaways, the impact of BLT on the future of large language models, and the broader implications of tokenizer‑free architectures.
subtopics: Recap of BLT’s three main advantages: compute efficiency, robustness, new scaling dimension
Implications for multilingual and low‑resource scenarios
Potential for hybrid token‑patch systems
Vision for a tokenizer‑free ecosystem
